Show whether a newer wdx is released, install it or roll it back.

```sh
wdx update [--apply | --rollback] [flags]
```

Without a flag nothing changes. `--apply` installs the newest release on the channel (the update.channel setting, or `--channel`); the daemon is stopped, the installed binary, a backup of the database and the config file are kept, and the daemon starts on the new binary. If any step fails, they are put back and the daemon starts on the old binary.

The release writes the config file anew, as its settings write does: the values set stay, its new settings are listed, and keys it no longer has are commented out at the end.

`--rollback` installs the kept version again, with the config file as it was before the update. The database stays when that version can use it; when a migration since the update breaks it, the backup is restored, losing every change since the update, which `--discard-changes` or the prompt agrees to, and `--cancel` refuses. Only one previous version is kept.

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--apply` |  | install the newest release on the channel |
| `--cancel` |  | with `--rollback`, change nothing without asking when the previous version needs the database backup restored |
| `--channel <channel>` | `stable` | follow this channel: stable or dev; the update.channel setting by default |
| `--discard-changes` |  | with `--rollback`, restore the database backup without asking when the previous version needs it |
| `--rollback` |  | install the version the last update replaced |
| `--version <version>` |  | this release version instead of the newest, such as 0.2.0 |

- at most one of `--apply` or `--rollback`
- at most one of `--discard-changes` or `--cancel`
- at most one of `--rollback` or `--channel`
- at most one of `--rollback` or `--version`
- with `--json` and `--rollback`: one of `--discard-changes` or `--cancel`

## Examples

```sh
# Show whether a newer release is available
wdx update

# Install it
wdx update --apply

# Install the newest dev release this once
wdx update --apply --channel dev

# Install one release
wdx update --apply --version 0.2.0

# Go back to the version the last update replaced
wdx update --rollback

# From a script, restoring the database backup if the previous version needs it
wdx update --rollback --discard-changes --json

# From a script, rolling back only if the database can stay
wdx update --rollback --cancel --json
```

## Output

Without a flag, the installed version, the newest on the channel and whether it is newer; with `--apply` or `--rollback`, the versions and schema versions before and after. With `--json`: {"update": {"current": ..., "latest": ..., "channel": ..., "available": ...}}, or {"result": ..., "update": {"from": ..., "to": ..., "channel": ..., "schema\_from": ..., "schema\_to": ..., "data\_restored": ..., "settings": {"added": [...], "dropped": [...]}}, "warnings": [...]}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `rolled_back`, `up_to_date` or `updated`.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`checksum_mismatch`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#checksum_mismatch) | 3 | the downloaded release does not match its checksum |
| [`download_failed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#download_failed) | 3 | the release could not be found or downloaded |
| [`no_previous_version`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#no_previous_version) | 1 | no previous version is kept to roll back to |
| [`older_version`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#older_version) | 1 | the release is older than the installed version |
| [`restore_required`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#restore_required) | 1 | rolling back needs the database backup, losing the changes since the update |
| [`settings_invalid`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#settings_invalid) | 1 | the release does not accept a value the config file sets |
| [`update_failed`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#update_failed) | 3 | the update or rollback failed and was undone |
| [`update_running`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#update_running) | 1 | another update or rollback is running |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |
